Colleagues 1,5,7,9,11,13 all decode the Morse preamble to a selection prompt about the origin of a quoted martial aria and read the quoted English rendering as something like “FAN CHIEF AND BANDITS … worthless to mention … one sword … block troops a million”. Segment 12 = .- -. -.. = AND and segment 13 = -... .- -. -.. .. - ... = BANDITS, and segment 10 = ..-. .- -. = FAN, segment 11 starts -.-. .... .. . ..-. = CHIEF. That matches the Chinese line “番邦小丑何足论，我一剑能挡百万兵 / 一剑能挡百万兵”, the famous Mu Guiying / 穆桂英挂帅 aria.

Baudot/ITA2 decoding is given as: 10101=Y, 00111=U, 00001=E, 00100=space, 01011=J, 00111=U. Hence option C 10101 00111 00001 00100 01011 00111 → Y U E [space] J U = “YUE JU”, i.e. 越剧. The same mapping is used by Colleagues 1,5,7,9,11,13 to link the aria to Yue opera.

Colleague 14 is the outlier, decoding E 01110 10100 00111 00011 01100 00100 01011 00111 as CHUAN [space] JU = 川剧/Chuanju and arguing the line is a Zhang Fei aria “范疆张达… 单凭一杆枪，能挡百万兵” centred in Sichuan. The Morse reconstruction in the thread points to “FAN CHIEF AND BANDITS”, i.e. the Mu Guiying “番王/番邦小丑” line, not the Zhang Fei “范疆张达” line, and the majority of colleagues associate that Mu Guiying aria with Yue opera.

Unresolved / to keep in mind: exact Morse tokenisation of segment 9 .-..-. - .... . and the punctuation around the opening quote is still messy, and a clean independent re-decode of the whole Morse string would confirm the English wording. For now the weight of evidence is for C = YUE JU, with E = CHUAN JU being the dissenting alternative.
